fullText.simplified:
第八章、再次见到楚怀王

    楚国与秦国的战争结束后，楚怀王派人来找我，说他要见我。
    “王为什么见我？”我问来人。
    “王要你去齐国，和齐国谈结盟的事。”
    我叹了一口气。是的，重新与齐国结盟，是楚国现在最好的选择。
    再见到楚怀王，他好像老了很多，头发也白了。我回想起八年前在兰台见到他，那时他还是个心中有理想、眼里有光的人，现在怎么就变成这样了？
    我看着他，苦笑了一下。没想到，他看着我，也苦笑了一下。我有点儿不理解，但很快就明白了。他在我的眼里已经变老了，我在他的眼里可能也变老了。
    “我读了《离骚》。虽然写得不错，但我不喜欢。”他说。
    我的苦笑变成了大笑，他也大声地笑了。在这笑声中我明白了，我们都变了，也都没有变。变的是样子，不变的是心中理想。虽然走了错路，但楚怀王要把楚国变强大的心没有变。
    我第二次去齐国。这一次没有上次那么顺利，齐王还在生气，但他最终还是答应了重新和楚国结盟。我从齐国的王宫出来，骑马往楚国跑。我兴奋地想要把这个好消息告诉楚怀王。
    就在快到引都时，我突然听到一个消息——秦国的张宜又来楚国了！
    原来，秦国知道了楚国想要重新和齐国结盟的事，他们又害怕了。秦王给楚怀王写信，说愿意送一些土地给楚国，希望楚国不要和齐国结盟。楚怀王回信说：“我不要土地，我只要张宜。”于是，张宜就一个人来到了楚国。
    我大概明白楚怀王为什么这么做，上次张宜骗了楚国，楚怀王一直很生气。现在张宜来了，一定要杀了这个小人！
fullText.traditional:
第八章、再次見到楚懷王

    楚國與秦國的戰爭結束後，楚懷王派人來找我，說他要見我。
    “王為什麼見我？”我問來人。
    “王要你去齊國，和齊國談結盟的事。”
    我嘆了一口氣。是的，重新與齊國結盟，是楚國現在最好的選擇。
    再見到楚懷王，他好像老了很多，頭髮也白了。我回想起八年前在蘭臺見到他，那時他還是個心中有理想、眼裡有光的人，現在怎麼就變成這樣了？
    我看著他，苦笑了一下。沒想到，他看著我，也苦笑了一下。我有點兒不理解，但很快就明白了。他在我的眼裡已經變老了，我在他的眼裡可能也變老了。
    “我讀了《離騷》。雖然寫得不錯，但我不喜歡。”他說。
    我的苦笑變成了大笑，他也大聲地笑了。在這笑聲中我明白了，我們都變了，也都沒有變。變的是樣子，不變的是心中理想。雖然走了錯路，但楚懷王要把楚國變強大的心沒有變。
    我第二次去齊國。這一次沒有上次那麼順利，齊王還在生氣，但他最終還是答應了重新和楚國結盟。我從齊國的王宮出來，騎馬往楚國跑。我興奮地想要把這個好消息告訴楚懷王。
    就在快到引都時，我突然聽到一個消息——秦國的張宜又來楚國了！
    原來，秦國知道了楚國想要重新和齊國結盟的事，他們又害怕了。秦王給楚懷王寫信，說願意送一些土地給楚國，希望楚國不要和齊國結盟。楚懷王回信說：“我不要土地，我只要張宜。”於是，張宜就一個人來到了楚國。
    我大概明白楚懷王為什麼這麼做，上次張宜騙了楚國，楚懷王一直很生氣。現在張宜來了，一定要殺了這個小人！

sentences.simplified: 楚国与秦国的战争结束后，楚怀王派人来找我，说他要见我。
sentences.traditional: 楚國與秦國的戰爭結束後，楚懷王派人來找我，說他要見我。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ guó yǔ qín guó de zhàn zhēng jié shù hòu chǔ huái wáng pài rén lái zhǎo wǒ shuō tā yào jiàn wǒ
sentences.english: After the war between Chu and Qin ended, King Huai of Chu sent someone to find me, saying he wanted to see me.

sentences.simplified: “王为什么见我？”我问来人。
sentences.traditional: “王為什麼見我？”我問來人。
sentences.pinyin: wáng wèi shén me jiàn wǒ wǒ wèn lái rén
sentences.english: “Why does the king want to see me?” I asked the messenger.

sentences.simplified: “王要你去齐国，和齐国谈结盟的事。”
sentences.traditional: “王要你去齊國，和齊國談結盟的事。”
sentences.pinyin: wáng yào nǐ qù qí guó hé qí guó tán jié méng de shì
sentences.english: “The king wants you to go to the state of Qi and discuss an alliance with them.”

sentences.simplified: 我叹了一口气。是的，重新与齐国结盟，是楚国现在最好的选择。
sentences.traditional: 我嘆了一口氣。是的，重新與齊國結盟，是楚國現在最好的選擇。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ tàn le yì kǒu qì shì de chóng xīn yǔ qí guó jié méng shì chǔ guó xiàn zài zuì hǎo de xuǎn zé
sentences.english: I sighed. Yes, re-establishing the alliance with Qi was the best choice for Chu now.

sentences.simplified: 再见到楚怀王，他好像老了很多，头发也白了。
sentences.traditional: 再見到楚懷王，他好像老了很多，頭髮也白了。
sentences.pinyin: zài jiàn dào chǔ huái wáng tā hǎo xiàng lǎo le hěn duō tóu fa yě bái le
sentences.english: When I saw King Huai of Chu again, he seemed to have aged a lot, and his hair had turned white.

sentences.simplified: 我回想起八年前在兰台见到他，
sentences.traditional: 我回想起八年前在蘭臺見到他，
sentences.pinyin: wǒ huí xiǎng qǐ bā nián qián zài lán tái jiàn dào tā
sentences.english: I recalled meeting him at the Orchid Terrace eight years previously.

sentences.simplified: 那时他还是个心中有理想、眼里有光的人，现在怎么就变成这样了？
sentences.traditional: 那時他還是個心中有理想、眼裡有光的人，現在怎麼就變成這樣了？
sentences.pinyin: nà shí tā hái shì ge xīn zhōng yǒu lǐ xiǎng yǎn lǐ yǒu guāng de rén xiàn zài zěn me jiù biàn chéng zhè yàng le
sentences.english: At that time, he was still a man with ideals in his heart and light in his eyes. How had he become like this?

sentences.simplified: 我看着他，苦笑了一下。没想到，他看着我，也苦笑了一下。
sentences.traditional: 我看著他，苦笑了一下。沒想到，他看著我，也苦笑了一下。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ kàn zhe tā kǔ xiào le yí xià méi xiǎng dào tā kàn zhe wǒ yě kǔ xiào le yí xià
sentences.english: I looked at him and gave a bitter smile. Unexpectedly, he looked at me and also gave a bitter smile.

sentences.simplified: 我有点儿不理解，但很快就明白了。他在我的眼里已经变老了，我在他的眼里可能也变老了。
sentences.traditional: 我有點兒不理解，但很快就明白了。他在我的眼裡已經變老了，我在他的眼裡可能也變老了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ yǒu diǎn'r bù lǐ jiě dàn hěn kuài jiù míng bai le tā zài wǒ de yǎn lǐ yǐ jīng biàn lǎo le wǒ zài tā de yǎn lǐ kě néng yě biàn lǎo le
sentences.english: I was a bit puzzled, but quickly understood. He had aged in my eyes, and I might also have aged in his eyes.

sentences.simplified: “我读了《离骚》。虽然写得不错，但我不喜欢。”他说。
sentences.traditional: “我讀了《離騷》。雖然寫得不錯，但我不喜歡。”他說。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ dú le lí sāo suī rán xiě de bú cuò dàn wǒ bù xǐ huan tā shuō
sentences.english: “I read ‘Sorrow at Parting’. Although it’s well-written, I don’t like it,” he said.

sentences.simplified: 我的苦笑变成了大笑，他也大声地笑了。
sentences.traditional: 我的苦笑變成了大笑，他也大聲地笑了。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de kǔ xiào biàn chéng le dà xiào tā yě dà shēng de xiào le
sentences.english: My bitter smile turned into laughter, and he laughed loudly too.

sentences.simplified: 在这笑声中我明白了，我们都变了，也都没有变。
sentences.traditional: 在這笑聲中我明白了，我們都變了，也都沒有變。
sentences.pinyin: zài zhè xiào shēng zhōng wǒ míng bai le wǒ men dōu biàn le yě dōu méi yǒu biàn
sentences.english: Amid that laughter, I realized that we had both changed and also not changed.

sentences.simplified: 变的是样子，不变的是心中理想。
sentences.traditional: 變的是樣子，不變的是心中理想。
sentences.pinyin: biàn de shì yàng zi bú biàn de shì xīn zhōng lǐ xiǎng
sentences.english: What had changed was our appearance; what had not changed were the ideals in our hearts.

sentences.simplified: 虽然走了错路，但楚怀王要把楚国变强大的心没有变。
sentences.traditional: 雖然走了錯路，但楚懷王要把楚國變強大的心沒有變。
sentences.pinyin: suī rán zǒu le cuò lù dàn chǔ huái wáng yào bǎ chǔ guó biàn qiáng dà de xīn méi yǒu biàn
sentences.english: Although he had taken the wrong path, King Huai of Chu’s desire to make Chu strong had not changed.

sentences.simplified: 我第二次去齐国。
sentences.traditional: 我第二次去齊國。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ dì èr cì qù qí guó
sentences.english: I went to Qi for the second time.

sentences.simplified: 这一次没有上次那么顺利，齐王还在生气，但他最终还是答应了重新和楚国结盟。
sentences.traditional: 這一次沒有上次那麼順利，齊王還在生氣，但他最終還是答應了重新和楚國結盟。
sentences.pinyin: zhè yí cì méi yǒu shàng cì nà me shùn lì qí wáng hái zài shēng qì dàn tā zuì zhōng hái shi dā ying le chóng xīn hé chǔ guó jié méng
sentences.english: This time was not as smooth as the last. The King of Qi was still angry, but he ultimately agreed to re-establish the alliance with Chu.

sentences.simplified: 我从齐国的王宫出来，骑马往楚国跑。我兴奋地想要把这个好消息告诉楚怀王。
sentences.traditional: 我從齊國的王宮出來，騎馬往楚國跑。我興奮地想要把這個好消息告訴楚懷王。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ cóng qí guó de wáng gōng chū lái qí mǎ wǎng chǔ guó pǎo wǒ xīng fèn de xiǎng yào bǎ zhè ge hǎo xiāo xi gào su chǔ huái wáng
sentences.english: I left the royal palace of Qi and rode back to Chu. I was excited to share this good news with King Huai of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 就在快到引都时，我突然听到一个消息——秦国的张宜又来楚国了！
sentences.traditional: 就在快到引都時，我突然聽到一個消息——秦國的張宜又來楚國了！
sentences.pinyin: jiù zài kuài dào yǐn dū shí wǒ tū rán tīng dào yí ge xiāo xi qín guó de zhāng yí yòu lái chǔ guó le
sentences.english: Just as I was about to reach Yindu, I suddenly heard some news—Zhang Yi of Qin had come to Chu again!

sentences.simplified: 原来，秦国知道了楚国想要重新和齐国结盟的事，他们又害怕了。
sentences.traditional: 原來，秦國知道了楚國想要重新和齊國結盟的事，他們又害怕了。
sentences.pinyin: yuán lái qín guó zhī dào le chǔ guó xiǎng yào chóng xīn hé qí guó jié méng de shì tā men yòu hài pà le
sentences.english: It turned out that Qin had learned about Chu’s intention to re-establish the alliance with Qi, and they were afraid.

sentences.simplified: 秦王给楚怀王写信，说愿意送一些土地给楚国，希望楚国不要和齐国结盟。
sentences.traditional: 秦王給楚懷王寫信，說願意送一些土地給楚國，希望楚國不要和齊國結盟。
sentences.pinyin: qín wáng gěi chǔ huái wáng xiě xìn shuō yuàn yì sòng yì xiē tǔ dì gěi chǔ guó xī wàng chǔ guó bú yào hé qí guó jié méng
sentences.english: The King of Qin wrote to King Huai of Chu, saying he was willing to give some land to Chu, hoping that Chu would not ally with Qi.

sentences.simplified: 楚怀王回信说：“我不要土地，我只要张宜。”于是，张宜就一个人来到了楚国。
sentences.traditional: 楚懷王回信說：“我不要土地，我只要張宜。”於是，張宜就一個人來到了楚國。
sentences.pinyin: chǔ huái wáng huí xìn shuō wǒ bú yào tǔ dì wǒ zhǐ yào zhāng yí yú shì zhāng yí jiù yí ge rén lái dào le chǔ guó
sentences.english: King Huai of Chu replied, “I don’t want land; I only want Zhang Yi.” And so, Zhang Yi came to Chu alone.

sentences.simplified: 我大概明白楚怀王为什么这么做，
sentences.traditional: 我大概明白楚懷王為什麼這麼做，
sentences.pinyin: wǒ dà gài míng bai chǔ huái wáng wèi shén me zhè me zuò
sentences.english: I roughly understood why King Huai of Chu did this.

sentences.simplified: 上次张宜骗了楚国，楚怀王一直很生气。
sentences.traditional: 上次張宜騙了楚國，楚懷王一直很生氣。
sentences.pinyin: shàng cì zhāng yí piàn le chǔ guó chǔ huái wáng yì zhí hěn shēng qì
sentences.english: Zhang Yi had deceived Chu previously, and King Huai of Chu had been very angry ever since.

sentences.simplified: 现在张宜来了，一定要杀了这个小人！
sentences.traditional: 現在張宜來了，一定要殺了這個小人！
sentences.pinyin: xiàn zài zhāng yí lái le yí dìng yào shā le zhè ge xiǎo rén
sentences.english: Now that Zhang Yi had come, he was definitely going to kill this scoundrel!

sentence_translations: Chapter 8: Meeting King Huai of Chu Again
After the war between Chu and Qin ended, King Huai of Chu sent someone to find me, saying he wanted to see me.
“Why does the king want to see me?” I asked the messenger.
“The king wants you to go to the state of Qi and discuss an alliance with them.”
I sighed. Yes, re-establishing the alliance with Qi was the best choice for Chu now.
When I saw King Huai of Chu again, he seemed to have aged a lot, and his hair had turned white.
I recalled meeting him at the Orchid Terrace eight years previously.
At that time, he was still a man with ideals in his heart and light in his eyes. How had he become like this?
I looked at him and gave a bitter smile. Unexpectedly, he looked at me and also gave a bitter smile.
I was a bit puzzled, but quickly understood. He had aged in my eyes, and I might also have aged in his eyes.
“I read ‘Sorrow at Parting’. Although it’s well-written, I don’t like it,” he said.
My bitter smile turned into laughter, and he laughed loudly too.
Amid that laughter, I realized that we had both changed and also not changed.
What had changed was our appearance; what had not changed were the ideals in our hearts.
Although he had taken the wrong path, King Huai of Chu’s desire to make Chu strong had not changed.
I went to Qi for the second time.
This time was not as smooth as the last. The King of Qi was still angry, but he ultimately agreed to re-establish the alliance with Chu.
I left the royal palace of Qi and rode back to Chu. I was excited to share this good news with King Huai of Chu.
Just as I was about to reach Yindu, I suddenly heard some news—Zhang Yi of Qin had come to Chu again!
It turned out that Qin had learned about Chu’s intention to re-establish the alliance with Qi, and they were afraid.
The King of Qin wrote to King Huai of Chu, saying he was willing to give some land to Chu, hoping that Chu would not ally with Qi.
King Huai of Chu replied, “I don’t want land; I only want Zhang Yi.” And so, Zhang Yi came to Chu alone.
I roughly understood why King Huai of Chu did this.
Zhang Yi had deceived Chu previously, and King Huai of Chu had been very angry ever since.
Now that Zhang Yi had come, he was definitely going to kill this scoundrel!
